response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Scope the retry-exhausted delete to SMS reminders

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43

Explanation:
The second `OR` branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method` filter. This SMS cron job will therefore delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount` exceeds 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders.

Today only this file increments `retryCount`, so nothing breaks yet. But `retryCount` is now a generic column on the shared model. As soon as another channel's cron (email or WhatsApp) uses it, this handler will silently delete that channel's reminders, possibly before that channel has finished its own retries.

Fix: add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retry branch.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
OR: [
  { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } },
  { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } },
],
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Reliability
Title: Failure inside the catch block aborts the whole batch

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189-199

Explanation:
`prisma.workflowReminder.update` is now awaited inside the `catch` block, and nothing guards it. If that update fails (for example a DB hiccup, or the row was deleted concurrently, which causes Prisma to throw P2025 "record not found"), the exception escapes the loop. Two things then go wrong:
- All remaining reminders in the run are skipped.
- The handler returns a 500 instead of `{ ok: true }`.

Before this change, errors were fully contained per reminder.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
} catch (error) {
  try {
    await prisma.workflowReminder.update({
      where: { id: reminder.id },
      data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
    });
  } catch (updateError) {
    console.log(`Failed to update retryCount for reminder ${reminder.id}: ${updateError}`);
  }
  console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`);
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Use an atomic increment for retryCount

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-186
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190-197

Explanation:
`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes back a value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap, both can read the same count, and one increment is lost. That reminder then gets retried more often than intended.

Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` performs the increment atomically in SQL and removes the dependency on the stale read. It also means `retryCount` would no longer need to be selected just to compute the new value.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Unclear retry limit and silent dropping of failed reminders

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39-41

Explanation:
The magic number `gt: 1` means a reminder gets two scheduling attempts (counts 0→1→2) and is then deleted. This is not documented, and it is easy to misread as "one retry".

The rows are also hard-deleted with no logging. When an SMS reminder permanently fails, there is no trace of why the attendee or host never received it.

Fix:
- Extract a named constant such as `MAX_SMS_RETRIES`.
- Log or record the reminders before deleting them, or mark them failed instead of deleting.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const MAX_SMS_SCHEDULE_ATTEMPTS = 2;
// ...
{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gte: MAX_SMS_SCHEDULE_ATTEMPTS } },
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Unindexed OR predicate on every cron run

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29-45
- packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000

Explanation:
The `deleteMany` now uses `OR` with a branch on the unindexed `retryCount` column. This branch has no `method` filter. That will typically force a sequential scan of the whole `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron invocation, and this table grows with every booking.

Adding the `method` filter to both branches (issue 1) helps. A composite index on `(method, retryCount)` would also help if the table is large. I have not verified the table's existing indexes beyond those shown in the diff.

Proposed fix:
~~~prisma
@@index([method, retryCount])
~~~
